craft_claim: Literary nonsense balances meaningful elements against nonsense elements; unmotivated absurdity without a base of sense is not the genre and reads as noise.

supporting_evidence.location: An Anatomy of Literary Nonsense (Rodopi, 1988), pp. 47-55, 166-167, 255
supporting_evidence.note: Tigges defines literary nonsense as balancing elements that make sense with elements that do not, and catalogues its devices: faulty cause and effect, portmanteau, neologism, reversals, imprecision, simultaneity, picture/text incongruity, arbitrariness, infinite repetition, mirroring, and misappropriation.
Ray keeps metre, rhyme, and syntax intact even as the content is absurd, so the nonsense reads as a rule-governed game rather than chaos.

scope: Invented language, portmanteau, and rule-governed absurdity in verse and prose.
exceptions: Dada and surrealist automatic writing pursue a different programme that deliberately voids sense; they should not be cited as evidence for this tone.
